## Incident Report — STRRAT RAT Infection (2024-07-30)

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 packets, 585.7s capture window). No separate IDS/alert export was present in the evidence directory — findings below are derived directly from packet analysis via tshark.

### 1. Infected host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.16.1.66 |
| MAC address | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F (NBNS/Kerberos confirmed; AD domain `wiresharkworkshop.online`, DC = WIRESHARK-WS-DC / 172.16.1.4) |
| Logged-in user | ccollier (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString and malware's own beacon field) |

### 2. Malware family

**STRRAT** — a Java-based backdoor/RAT.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The malware's own C2 heartbeat traffic contains a plaintext, pipe-delimited beacon that literally names itself:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<base64 window title>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

Field breakdown: literal string `STRRAT`, client ID `1BE8292C`, hostname, username, OS (Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit), installed AV (Windows Defender), base64-encoded active window title, client/build version `1.6`, geolocation string, "Not Installed" flag, and an uptime counter. This is STRRAT's known check-in format — not an inference from behavior alone.

The base64 blob decodes to `pounds-formula [Compatibility Mode] - PowerPoint`, indicating the victim had a file named **"pounds-formula"** open in PowerPoint at time of infection — consistent with a malicious Office-document lure as the delivery vector (the delivery/download itself is not present in this capture; the pcap begins with the implant already beaconing).

### 3. Indicators of compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` — sole C2 endpoint. Direct IP connection (TCP stream 83, no DNS resolution observed — IP is hardcoded in the implant). Beacon starts at t=76.99s and repeats roughly every 5 seconds through the end of the capture (t=585.66s), each check-in preceded by a fixed 7-byte length-prefix packet followed by the pipe-delimited status string. No inbound C2 commands/tasking were observed in this capture window (server side only ACKs, sends no payload data).

**Malicious domains:** None — the implant communicates via hardcoded IP, no DNS lookups for the C2 were captured.

**Malicious URLs:** None observed (no HTTP/S request pointed at 141.98.10.79 or any other non-benign destination; the only HTTP traffic in the capture is legitimate — Microsoft NCSI connectivity check to `www.msftconnecttest.com` and a benign `ip-api.com` geolocation lookup, both of which are consistent with STRRAT self-profiling behavior but are not malicious infrastructure themselves).

**Transferred files / hashes:** None recoverable. No malware payload, dropper, or document was transferred over any protocol visible in this pcap (HTTP object export yielded only benign OS/browser artifacts: `connecttest.txt`, JSON telemetry, favicon/cert-revocation objects). Consequently no SHA256 can be computed from this evidence — the infection predates the start of the capture.

**Supporting/benign context (not IOCs, but relevant):** DNS queries to `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com`, `repo1.maven.org`, `github.com`/`objects.githubusercontent.com`, and a large (~8.8 MB) download from Fastly IP 199.232.196.209 (SNI `repo1.maven.org`) are consistent with STRRAT's dependency on a Java runtime, but attribution to the malware could not be confirmed from traffic content alone — these are treated as environmental noise, not confirmed IOCs.

### Summary
Host DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as domain user **ccollier**, is actively beaconing to a **STRRAT** RAT C2 at **141.98.10.79:12132** throughout the entire capture, self-identifying via its native check-in protocol. Recommend isolating the host immediately, resetting ccollier's credentials, and hunting for the STRRAT jar/persistence artifact (typically a scheduled task or startup entry launching a `.jar` via `wscript`/`javaw`) since the delivery mechanism (likely the "pounds-formula" PowerPoint lure) is not captured in this pcap.
